text: The Bardo Museum in Tunisia was the site of the killing of 23 or more gunmen. The Bardo National Museum in Tunisia was attacked by gunmen on Wednesday, resulting in the death of at least 23 people. This was a tragic incident as it targeted a well-known cultural landmark and the key to the country's economy that relies on tourism. The majority of those who lost their lives were non-native individuals, with many having arrived from cruise ships docked in Tunis earlier that day. Two of the attackers were killed by security forces during a standoff inside the museum, and numerous individuals were treated for injuries. Adjacent to the national parliament is the Bardo, home of one of the world's great collections of Roman mosaics. The assault has jolted a nation that is frequently cited as the sole triumph of the Arab Spring. Following the 2011 uprising that removed President Zine El Abidine Ben Ali from power, Tunisia has implemented a new constitution and conducted free elections. Despite this, it has become a significant source of foreign fighters for extremist groups in Syria and Iraq, with an estimated 3,000 Tunisians believed to have joined them. Those two facts are inseparable to Mabrouka M'Barek, a former member of Tunisia's National Constituent Assembly. She believes that Tunisia's failure to "recruit" its own citizens into society has resulted in many young people, particularly in the country's less affluent interior, feeling excluded from the new democracy. She contends that when the state denies them a place, extremist groups are eager to provide one. Her argument shifts the focus from policing to unemployment, regional inequality, and political exclusion, which were the root causes of the 2011 uprising. The government of Tunisia has promised a strong response, and investigators are working to identify the perpetrators of the attack. As Tunisia mourns the loss, many are questioning the potential of their democratic youth to make a mark on the next generation before they turn their attention.

Lunch will be served, and we're aiming to finish by 2:00 p.m. Please send an RSVP by Friday, April 5th by reaching out to our office at (608) 555-0142.
